title: He Walked Into the Clinic Talking, Yet Scans Showed His Self Network in Deep Anesthesia

acts.name: 1880 Paris Consultation & Mademoiselle X's Hollow Body Paradox
sentences: You think a talking patient always feels alive inside!
Yet he walked in swearing his brain had vanished!
Doctors first saw this in Patient Graham's brain scan.
Panic surged inside a waking brain.
In eighteen eighty, Paris doctor Jules Cotard met Mademoiselle X.
At forty three, her pulse beat under his stethoscope.
Still, she swore she had no brain or stomach!
Feeling zero organs inside, she refused all food!
She claimed she could never die — and that wasn't the strangest part.

acts.name: 1995 Berrios 100-Case Audit & Silenced Insular Vitality
sentences: Does each patient with this syndrome claim to be dead?
In nineteen ninety five, German Berrios checked one hundred cases.
Only fifty five percent denied life, like a coin toss!
Eighty six percent denied owning organs, like an empty suitcase!
Three profiles emerged, including one group with zero sadness.
What cuts off your inner sense of life?
Deep inside, your insula, your gut-feeling center, hums nonstop.
When that insula, goes silent, you feel hollow!
Living feeling empty was a total nightmare.

acts.name: Two-Factor Belief Failure & The 1996 Capgras-Cotard Mirror Flip
sentences: Why does a tired body know it is alive?
Your dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, your mental scratchpad, checks wild thoughts.
Factor one mutes warmth, like a broken fuel gauge!
Factor two breaks logic testing, accepting an blocked story.
Instead of feeling numb, the mind concludes I vanished!
In nineteen ninety six, Andrew Young spotted its mirror twin.
Both cut warmth from the amygdala, your alarm!
Blame others and family looks fake — blame yourself and you vanish!
But here's the twist: what showed up on Graham's brain scan?

acts.name: 2013 Patient Graham's Anesthesia-Level Self-Network Scan
sentences: In twenty thirteen, brain doctors in Europe studied patient Graham.
He walked into the clinic speaking with clear, words.
Plainly, he told doctors his brain no longer existed.
Doctors checked his default mode network, his daydream network.
Across his parietal cortex, his spatial map, energy plunged!
His brain looked like deep deep sleep, like a dark house!
How could Graham talk clear with a sleeping self-network?
Was this rare delusion a lifelong curse with zero hope?

acts.name: 48-Hour Dialysis Reversal & Graham's Full Clinical Recovery
sentences: Doctors found this eerie delusion is often reversible!
Kidney patients took cold-sore pills and woke up hollow.
Drug buildup muted their inner hum overnight!
Dialysis cleared their blood in forty-eight hours, like a clean filter!
One hundred percent woke up normal, like a bright lamp!
Medical care also switched Graham's self-network back on!
That test revealed a hidden survival rule.
Graham walked outside again and enjoyed daily life.

Protect sleep, water, and kidney pill safety each day.
